scope: 1980s–12 October 2026 UI aesthetics history, native-language examples, graphic influences and earlier foundations.
chronologyPolicy: orderBandStart is an approximate sorting boundary, never an asserted invention year.
Exact event dates are separately typed and sourced. They can be release, announcement, naming, publication or example dates.
Cultural artifact periods do not establish UI adoption or popularity.
Cross-period directions and unresolved origins remain undated rather than being invented for sorting.
Referenced era, revival date, software-version date, source date and screenshot creation date are different.
Aesthetic recognition and UI relevance are separate from quality and the future allowed vocabulary.

records.name: Laser Grid / corporate high-tech graphic world
records.definition: Neon grids and reflective synthetic forms construct a coordinated high-tech graphic world.
counterexamples: Synthwave revival assumed to be an original 1980s UI
records.limits: No specific original UI frame was inspected. A referenced decade and the date a revival/name emerged are different facts.

records.name: Memphis-Milano graphic influence
records.definition: Playful geometric color and juxtaposition form a recognizable postmodern design influence.
counterexamples: Furniture history treated as a 1981 GUI release
records.limits: The design movement predates many web adaptations. No original UI was inspected under this exact label; keep graphic influence distinct from UI introduction.

records.name: Pixel / arcade
records.dateBasis: reference era with later archived UI examples
records.datingLimit: The 1980 ordering denotes a reference-era bin, not the invention of pixel art or a first web deployment.

records.name: Terminal / character-grid UI
records.definition: A character grid makes text, selection and command structure the primary interface material.
records.limits: DOS/PC context is documented in 1981. This does not date the invention of terminals, ANSI art or all text UI; no terminal screen was visually reviewed here.

records.name: Monochrome bitmap desktop
records.definition: One-bit graphics organize a paper-like workspace with pictorial objects and compact window controls.

events.event: Star introduction reported by its designers

records.limits: Inspected ViewPoint is a successor illustration from the 1989 retrospective; System 1.1 is a later rendering of historical software. Neither is claimed as a launch-day screenshot.

records.name: Amiga Workbench 1.x
records.definition: A named limited-color desktop uses bitmap labels, outlined windows and pictorial drawers/tools.
records.limits: Source provenance establishes this platform. A later PNG of old software is not a file created in 1985; palette-selection motives were not independently verified.

records.name: Windows 1.x tiled color GUI
records.definition: Early Windows supplies a limited-color graphical operating environment for DOS applications.
records.limits: No Windows 1.x frame was visually inspected in this revision. The release is verified; detailed version-specific styling remains a comparison lead.

records.name: Frasurbane
records.definition: Classical/refined typography and staged cultural imagery form a particular consumer-era visual world.
records.limits: The ordering year represents a broad late-decade bin. UI use under this exact name is unverified in this corpus; do not promote it just because a page has a serif.

records.name: Global Village Coffeehouse
records.definition: Handmade/woodcut-like graphic relationships construct a particular idealized communal visual world.
records.limits: Graphic/consumer context is documented; no original interface under this exact label was visually inspected. Cultural imagery must not establish a creator’s identity or values.

records.name: LCARS / Okudagram instrumentation
records.definition: A fictional information system presents complex instrumentation through a strong graphic organizing grammar.
counterexamples: Believable prop graphics treated as usable software

events.event: Original TNG panels dated by their designers

records.limits: Creator intent concerns convincing screen scenery. No functional LCARS workflow was tested, and it is not an alias for every neon HUD.

records.name: Utopian Scholastic / edutainment imagery
records.definition: Educational collage and idealized subject imagery combine into a distinctive reference world.
records.limits: Encartacore is archive terminology, not automatic interface evidence. A photographed object and the surrounding UI need independent description.

records.name: OPEN LOOK workstation UI
records.definition: A named workstation look-and-feel belongs to the early X/UNIX interface branch.
counterexamples: All X applications called OPEN LOOK
A toolkit name proving one screenshot style
records.limits: Period articles establish the branch, but the original manual and detailed control visuals were not inspected; round-button recipes are not asserted from an unread manual.

records.name: Classic beveled desktop UI
records.definition: Raised and inset edges distinguish actions and fields within compact window/menu systems.
counterexamples: Neumorphic low relief treated as the same grammar
records.limits: The visual example is Windows 95; this is not a claim that Windows 95 invented bevels. Function, metaphor and material need separate labels.

records.name: Motif / later CDE workstation branch
records.periodLabel: Around 1989 for Motif; later CDE development
records.definition: A specified look-and-feel and toolkit coordinate workstation applications; later desktop integration is a related milestone.
counterexamples: X Window System treated as one aesthetic
records.limits: The maintainer FAQ dates Motif around 1989. CDE is a related later context, not a simultaneous 1989 introduction; no first CDE release date is asserted here.

records.name: NeXTSTEP workstation language
records.definition: A named workstation interface combines object-oriented application structure with a coordinated desktop/control language.
counterexamples: A black computer chassis treated as UI evidence
records.limits: The original manual fetch was forbidden and no NeXT desktop frame was inspected. Exact bevel/font prescriptions remain unverified in this study.

records.name: Early hypertext / document web
records.definition: Documents, headings and linked text provide the visible structure before elaborate branded chrome.
counterexamples: Missing CSS treated as deliberate style
records.limits: The museum includes the 1991 web context. A document-oriented interface is a historical form, not proof of intentional contemporary brutalism.

records.name: Gen X Soft Club
records.datingLimit: This broad current period is preserved rather than reduced to an unsupported exact year. UI examples under the exact label remain unverified.

records.name: Raw web brutalism
records.periodLabel: Older raw-web precedents; documented style debate in 2017
records.dateBasis: precedent period and later terminology discussion
records.datingLimit: Early HTML is a precedent, not necessarily deliberate brutalism. This is not a single verified origin date.

records.name: BeOS tabbed desktop language
records.definition: A short tab marks the active window while compact native controls retain a coherent desktop grammar.
counterexamples: All classic gray UI called BeOS
records.limits: The reviewed frame is R5, not proof of a 1995 first appearance. The exact first-use date of tabs remains unverified; source ordering is approximate.

records.name: Directory / portal web
records.definition: Groups of links and categories make a collection/service navigable within a compact page.
counterexamples: Every personal GeoCities site treated as a portal
All link lists called an aesthetic
records.limits: Portal is partly an experience/composition form. It should not become a visual identity without additional evidence; the hosted personal sites are a separate corpus.

records.name: Early handheld / PDA utility UI
records.definition: Compact pen/touch tasks establish a handheld UI branch before smartphone glass and app-store-era visuals.
counterexamples: Mobile UI assumed to begin in 2007
A phone-shaped marketing mockup proving handheld interaction
records.limits: No complete Palm application was visually inspected. This is a relevant platform/task branch, not a new aesthetic filter or a first-ever touchscreen claim.

records.name: Grunge / distressed web
records.definition: Distressed typography, imperfect textures and cutout relationships deliberately shape a web composition.

events.event: Practitioner commentary on grunge and gloss

records.limits: The 1996 frame is centered and spacious, with disturbance concentrated in type/imagery. A 2008 trend article is not the style origin.

records.name: Y2K futurism
records.dateBasis: curator artifact period corroborated by archived UI
records.datingLimit: CARI’s category period currently conflicts with its history narrative. The broader period is approximate; original versus revival needs provenance.

records.name: Metalheart
records.dateBasis: curator period plus archived UI collection
records.datingLimit: A concrete UI corpus is now linked. No uninspected entry is granted visual claims merely from collection membership.

records.name: Platinum / Mac OS 8 appearance
records.definition: A named gray dimensional control system coordinates frames, accents and system typography.

events.event: Dated manual page for Platinum appearance

records.limits: Inspected original manual figure. The documentation date is not a retail-release date; manual text distinguishes layout from appearance.

records.name: Skinned media-player UI
records.definition: An application retains actions while its chrome, readouts and imagery are repainted into many visual worlds.
counterexamples: Museum launch treated as player-skin invention
records.limits: The late-1990s ordering is an approximate historical context, not an independently verified first skin date. Skin-level classification is required; the corpus is visually diverse.

records.name: Vectorheart
records.datingLimit: The old archive definition is visually specific, but an independently inspected interface under the exact label remains needed.

records.name: Technical / immersive Flash-era web
records.definition: Compact technical navigation frames layered digital imagery into an immersive branded website.
counterexamples: Flash technology treated as one aesthetic
A still assumed to prove motion
records.limits: Founding and version dates differ. The inspected v1 frame supports technical millennium language; specific Metalheart attribution needs that version’s evidence rather than all studio work inheriting it.

records.name: Apple Aqua
records.datingLimit: This is a design introduction, not every later OS X release. The inspected 2001 website shares period presentation but is not proof of native Aqua implementation.

records.name: Frutiger Metro / vector-pop nostalgia
records.datingLimit: This is not Microsoft Metro. No verified naming date or production UI corpus was established.

records.name: McBling
records.datingLimit: Fashion/consumer excess does not establish a UI’s aesthetic from one pink/chrome asset; no production UI was verified under this exact label.

records.name: Scene / MySpace-era grunge
records.periodLabel: 2000s reference world; precise UI corpus unresolved
records.datingLimit: MySpace-era cultural references are not one aesthetic shared by all profile pages; no exact first naming date is asserted.

records.name: Synthwave / outrun
records.datingLimit: Ordering is deliberately coarse: exact visual/UI origin was not established. Related music/graphic names are not forced into one canonical synonym.

records.name: Luna / Windows XP visual language
records.definition: Opaque colorful native presentation gives the desktop a softer consumer-facing identity.
counterexamples: Later Royale imagery claimed as original Luna
records.limits: Inspected a later-published XP login illustration. The source also contains a Royale-named asset; it was not used to assert the exact 2001 Luna desktop.

records.name: Frutiger Aero
records.dateBasis: curator artifact period and retrospective naming

events.event: Original public group/naming event in CARI history

records.datingLimit: Current CARI credits Sofi Xian and Froyo Tam jointly; widely repeated 2017 naming claims differ. The reviewed Aero-era UI is a related artifact, not an exact alias for the whole aesthetic.

records.name: Frutiger Eco
records.datingLimit: The UI branch and first coining date remain unsettled; ecological imagery does not establish sustainable performance.

records.name: Glossy Web 2.0 visual treatment
records.definition: Rounded dimensional surfaces, highlights and bright typographic branding shape a web presentation.
counterexamples: Web 2.0 technical meaning treated as visual birthdate
records.limits: The 2004 ordering is an approximate mid-2000s period boundary, not an origin date. Web 2.0’s social/technical history and this glossy visual subset are different.

records.name: Windows Aero / Aero Glass
records.dateBasis: approximate development period with implementation documentation
records.definition: Native translucent window chrome creates a glass-like layer over the desktop.
counterexamples: Every glass treatment claimed as Windows Aero
records.limits: The inspected image is a Windows 7 pre-release frame, not Vista launch output. Development-era ordering is approximate; Frutiger Aero is a broader retrospective aesthetic, not the native implementation’s alias.

records.name: Superflat Pop
records.definition: A pop-commercial interpretation of Japanese Superflat imagery combines bright character/graphic relationships.
records.limits: This is not an alias for flat UI. No production interface was verified under this exact cultural label.

records.name: Oxygen / KDE 4 artwork
records.definition: A coordinated desktop artwork/control language forms a named native visual system.
counterexamples: Desktop renderer treated as aesthetic identity
records.limits: Release text was read, not a complete Oxygen screenshot set. Detailed visual recipes need image comparisons before classification.

records.name: Flat
records.periodLabel: Planar predecessors; modern UI movement documented in early 2010s
records.dateBasis: modern movement context with older rendering roots

events.event: iOS 7 announcement as one major UI milestone

records.datingLimit: Flat surfaces existed earlier. Metro, iOS 7, minimalism and the whole Material system are not aliases for flat design.

records.name: Hexatron / futuristic HUD
records.datingLimit: The related project is not asserted to be the first Hexatron artifact or a usable production application.

records.name: Metro / Windows Phone typography-led UI
records.definition: Typography and content replace much decorative chrome through a coordinated navigation language.
counterexamples: Frutiger Metro treated as Microsoft’s system
records.limits: This verifies a naming/UI milestone, not the first precursor in Zune or Windows Media Center. No interaction was tested.

records.name: Polychrome / fluid-color imagery
records.datingLimit: Period estimates concern reference artifacts or documented use; they do not establish first-ever UI use.

records.name: Seapunk
records.datingLimit: The interview date is not a proven first-use date. Aquatic motifs alone are insufficient for a UI claim.

records.name: Semi-flat / selective depth
records.periodLabel: 2010s practitioner vocabulary; selective depth has older precedents

records.name: Solarpunk / eco-futurism
records.datingLimit: A formative post is not sole invention. UI evidence under this exact visual world remains unverified; green branding alone is insufficient.

records.name: Vaporwave
records.datingLimit: Referenced consumer imagery often dates to the 1980s/1990s. Its age is not the date vaporwave emerged; no named production UI was inspected.

records.name: Adwaita / adaptive GNOME visual language
records.definition: A coordinated application/control system evolves toward clearer native hierarchy and adaptive layouts.
counterexamples: All GTK versions treated as identical
records.limits: These are separate milestones. No first-ever Adwaita coining date or complete application adoption date is asserted.

records.name: Blob World
records.datingLimit: Soft rendered worlds and actual rounded controls differ. The broad ordering is an approximate bin, not the first blob or a verified 2014 UI release.

records.name: Breeze / Plasma 5 visual language
records.definition: Flatter native theming and typographic emphasis simplify a desktop artwork system.
counterexamples: Flat assumed to mean no hierarchy
Every Plasma 5 component assumed fully migrated on day one
records.limits: The release describes gradual completion; it does not prove immediate uniformity of all controls.

records.name: Corporate expressive illustration
records.datingLimit: Corporate Memphis is a related archive term, not a synonym for all illustration; the date does not establish Alegria’s creator/system history.

records.name: Material Design
records.datingLimit: The paper/spatial system is not entirely flat; 2018 and 2021 changes are subsequent milestones rather than invented aesthetic births.

records.name: Austurbane
records.datingLimit: Period estimates concern reference artifacts or documented use; they do not establish first-ever UI use.

records.name: Fluent material system

records.datingLimit: Acrylic, Mica and dimming have different material roles. Do not backdate current Fluent 2 guidance or Mica to this announcement.

records.name: Neo-Vectorheart
records.datingLimit: Period estimates concern reference artifacts or documented use; they do not establish first-ever UI use.

records.name: Neo-Y2K
records.datingLimit: Earlier research/art events and the curator’s strongest-relevance interval are different. No production UI was verified under this exact variant name.

records.name: Refined tech
records.dateBasis: operational synthesis with related archive period
records.datingLimit: Cyberbougie is a related archive label. This ordering bin does not date a universal refined-tech movement or make Fluent/glass/neumorphism synonyms.

records.name: Neumorphism
records.datingLimit: This visible date is preferred to secondary citations giving 16 December. The inspected diagram establishes low-relief material, not production prevalence.

records.name: Big Sur’s renewed dimensional macOS UI
records.definition: Apple reworks desktop depth, control shapes and presentation within a named operating-system design.
counterexamples: Every rounded macOS icon called neumorphic
records.limits: Announcement and public availability differ. A relation to soft dimensional styling is not a blanket neumorphism classification.

records.name: Glassmorphism
records.periodLabel: Earlier translucent UI; named article in November 2020
records.datingLimit: The naming date is not the invention of glass-like UI. The inspected concept card is not verified banking software.

records.name: Neobrutalism

events.event: Gumroad announces new brand and website

records.datingLimit: The rebrand date does not establish the first coiner; aesthetic attribution is supported separately by UI analysis, not by this short announcement alone.

records.name: Claymorphism
records.periodLabel: 2021 named creator discussion; older inflated/tactile imagery
records.datingLimit: These are documented terminology milestones, not the first rounded 3D objects. The inspected dashboard montage is a concept illustration.

records.name: Material You / adaptive-personal Material

A static theme proving dynamic personalization
records.limits: Generic visual traits can be observed separately. Actual dynamic behavior requires more than one still.

records.name: Windows 11 / rounded Fluent and Mica

records.limits: The date is an account, not first availability. Mica is opaque; the platform cannot be established from blur alone.

records.name: visionOS spatial UI
records.definition: A named native system places application content and controls within a spatial computing environment.
counterexamples: A static glass rectangle proving spatial interaction
records.limits: Not the beginning of all spatial UI and not the 2024 consumer release. No headset task or motion state was tested.

records.name: Apple Liquid Glass

records.datingLimit: Native provenance is stronger than appearance resemblance. Adaptive optics/motion were not established from a screenshot.

records.name: Cybersigilism
records.dateBasis: dated discussion and project, not origin
records.datingLimit: This dates one project, not the first use of the name or a deployed UI design language.

records.name: Material 3 Expressive
records.datingLimit: The inspected frame covers part of the published plate. Announcement, beta, rollout and actual product adoption are different dates.

records.name: Y3K / speculative hyper-futurism

records.name: Acid graphics / digital rave

records.name: Anti-design

records.name: Cinematic
